questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which part of the basal ganglia receives the afferent input?
questions.explanation:
The striatum xéceives the afferent input.
Note:

There are two main inputs to the basal ganglia: From the cerebral cortex (corticostriate pathway)
and from the thalamus (thalamostriate pathway). They are both excitatory (glutamate) and they
both terminate in the striatum.

The two major outputs of the basal ganglia are from GPi and substantia nigra. Both are inhibitory
(GABAergic) and both project to the thalamus

From the thalamus, there is an excitatory (glutamatergic) projection to the prefrontal and
premotor cortex. This completes the cortical-basal ganglia-thalamic-cortical loop

questions.question: Efferent from cerebellar cortex is through which cell:
questions.explanation:
Purkinje cells‘ae the only output neurons (efferent neurons) from the cerebellar cortex.

The Purkinje cells are the largest neurons in the cerebellum. Their axons, which are the only
output from the cerebellar cortex, project to the deep cerebellar nuclei, especially the dentate
nucleus, where they form inhibitory synapses

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the neocerebellum?

options.text: Planning and programming of voluntary movements

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning and programming of voluntary movements
questions.explanation:
The function of the neocerebellum is planning and programming of voluntary movements.
The cerebellum can be divided into:
The Vestibulocerebellum/Archicerebellum: Consists principally of the flocculonodular lobe and adjacent portions of the vermis. It participates in balance, vestibular reflexes, and eye movements.
The Spinocerebellum/Paleocerebellum: Consists of most of the vermis plus the adjacent intermediate zones on both sides of the vermis. It coordinates movements of the limbs. Vermis: Proximal muscles, Intermediate zones: Distal muscles.
The Cerebrocerebellum/neocerebellum: Consists of the large lateral zones of the cerebellar hemispheres. It receives all its input from the cerebral cortex (motor, premotor and somatosensory). It transmits its output back to the brain, functioning in a feedback manner to plan sequential voluntary body and limb movements.

A patient with a suspected cerebellar lesion will not have resting tremors, Resting tremors are
characteristic features of basal ganglia lesions. (Parkinson's disease)

Intentional tremors are seen in cerebellar diseases

Features of cerebellar disease

* Ataxia - Incoordinated, intermittent jerky movements with drunken gait
« Hypotonia or atonia — Reduced or absence of muscle tone

« Dysmetria - Inability to judge the force and range of movement resulting in past pointing
« Dysdiad okokinesia — Failure to perform rapid alternating movements.

+ Decomposition of movement - Lack of smooth flow of movement.

« Speech defect - Staccato speech or slurring speech

+ Pendular knee jerk (a feature of hypotonia)

+ Intention tremors.

« Nystagmus (jerky movements of the eye)

«Rebound phenomenon

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following fibres reach the Purkinje cell directly?
questions.explanation:
The fibres of inferior olivary nucleus (climbing fibres) reach the purkinje cell directly
Note:

The input from the Purkinje cells to the deep nuclei is inhibitory.

However, the deep nuclei output is always excitatory.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Molecular layer contains stellate and basket cells
Molecular is the innermost layer of cortex
Axons of Purkinje cell secrete Glutamate on deep cerebellar nuclei

questions.correctAnswerText: Molecular layer contains stellate and basket cells
questions.explanation:
The cerebellar cortex has three layers:

External molecular layer: Contains Basket and Stellate Cells

Purkinje cell layer: Only one cell thick, containing the purkinje cells

Internal granular layer: Contains Granule and Golgi Cells

questions.question: Which of the following ascending pathways enters the cerebellum through the peduncle highlighted in green in the image?
questions.explanation:
The peduncle highlighted in the image is the superior cerebellar peduncle. The anterior
spinocerebellar tract enters the cerebellum through it and terminates in both sides of the
cerebellum

Dorsal spinocerebellar tract enters the cerebellum through the inferior cerebellar peduncle and
terminates on the same side as its origin

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Inhibition of Purkinje cells by stellate cells is an example of _____.

options.text: Stellate cells doesn’t inhibit Purkinje cells

questions.explanation:
Inhibition of Purkinje cells by stellate cells is an example of feedforward inhibition.

Mossy fibers exert a weak excitatory effect on many Purkinje cells via the granule cells. The
granule cells also excite the basket and stellate cells via their parallel fibers. The basket and
stellate cells, in turn, inhibit the Purkinje cells (Feed forward inhibition)

Renshaw cells exhibit feed back inhibition.
